en: Jātaka Chakkanipāta, Avāriyavagga (The Section on the Unrestrained)
3. The Darīmukha Jātaka:
“Sensual pleasures are mud and sensual pleasures are a mire;
this fear has been declared to have three roots.”
“Dust and smoke have been proclaimed by me;
abandon them and go forth, O Brahmadatta!
“Attached, impassioned, and infatuated,” [he said].
“O Brahmin, I feel a sense of revulsion toward sensual pleasures;
though I am driven by the need for a livelihood, I cannot bring myself to abandon them.
Yet, I shall perform abundant meritorious deeds.”
“He who, when being exhorted by one who desires his welfare and is compassionate for his benefit,
does not follow the instruction,
thinking, ‘This alone is better’— ”
The dull-witted one enters the womb again and again;
he goes to a terrifying hell,
filled with both the beautiful and the ugly, and full of urine and excrement.
“Beings who are greedy do not abandon their own bodies,
those who remain with unremoved passion for sensual pleasures.
“Smeared with filth and bespattered with blood,”
Smeared with phlegm, they emerge;
for whatever they touch with their bodies,
all of it is entirely unpleasant and nothing but suffering.
Having seen this, I declare that I have no other source [of knowledge]:
I remember my many former births through various well-spoken verses.
“Darīmukha caused Sumedha to reflect.
Thus ends the third Jātaka, the Darīmukha Jātaka.
